title: Move a Note by dragging, with Raise
lede: The Drag engine, written once: a press becomes a Drag past a 3 px Dead zone, the Preview is a `translate` written straight from each event, and the one way out, `end()`, either resets and dispatches one `move` or resets and saves nothing. Resize (#5) will reuse all of it with a new Drag kind.

scenarios.name: Drag a Note and release it

steps.title: pointerdown on the Note
steps.explain: Raise first, so the Note is in front before it moves and stays there for the whole Drag. Then `start` gets the Note **as rendered**: that is the `from` rect every delta is added to.

steps.title: start filters, captures, presses
steps.explain: The Note gets the scroll container from `BoardDomContext`, which App provides with a value that never changes, so reading it renders nothing. `preventDefault` stops focus moves, text selection and native drags. Capture keeps hover and double-clicks off the neighbours. The controller then records the press point and the scroll position, and attaches every listener in one `listen`. Nothing is drawn yet: the press is pending.

steps.title: pointermove past the Dead zone
steps.explain: While the delta stays within 3 px nothing is written, so a click never nudges a Note. Past it, `pending` turns off for good, and the Preview is written **synchronously**: no rAF, so it is never a frame behind the pointer. It is a `translate`, which only composites.

steps.title: pointerup
steps.explain: `end(true)` detaches and releases capture, then computes the action from the **same** maths the Preview used, so the drop is exactly what was shown. The Preview is reset **before** the dispatch: the store update re-renders the Note with new `left/top` before the next paint, so it lands where the Preview was. Dispatching first would briefly add the old translate to the new position. (No flicker was seen in the tests; that ordering wasn't measured frame by frame.)

run.to: return { type: 'move', id: from.id, x, y };

steps.title: Only that Note re-renders
steps.explain: `withNote` replaces one Note and keeps `ids` and the rest by reference, so the Board and Note *b* see no change. The browser test wraps each Note in a `<Profiler>` (test-only, through App) and checks that only *a* rendered.

steps.title: The container scrolls; the pointer is still
steps.explain: The Board moves under the pointer, so the delta adds the scroll since the press. The scroll listener calls `update` too, so the Note follows the Board without waiting for a pointer move.

scenarios.name: A click: release inside the Dead zone

steps.title: pointerup while pending
steps.explain: `end` returns before writing or dispatching anything: a click saves nothing. Editing will hook in here later, since a click enters it.

steps.title: Any cancel goes through end(false)
steps.explain: All three revert the Preview and dispatch nothing. `end` clears `session` first, so a second signal (another Escape, a late `pointerup`) finds nothing to end: one detach, at most one dispatch.

scenarios.name: A release the page never saw

steps.title: pointermove with no button down
steps.explain: If the button came up outside the window, the next move arrives with `buttons === 0`. The controller treats it as the missed release and commits where the pointer is, so the Note doesn't stay stuck to it. `lostpointercapture` is deliberately not a signal: Chrome can fire it before a valid `pointerup`.

scenarios.name: How the browser tests press the mouse

steps.title: A test calls drag(locator, { dx, dy })
steps.explain: Synthetic `PointerEvent`s can't take pointer capture, so the test runs a command in Node that drives Playwright's real mouse. The test iframe is scaled down to fit the window, so every client point is multiplied by the iframe's scale and offset by its box.

notes.title: No Trash zone in `io` yet
notes.detail: The spec's `DragIO` has `trashRect()` and `setOverTrash()`, and the kind context has `trashRect`. They are left out until #6 adds the Trash zone, which may be cut. Adding them then is additive.

notes.title: The controller is created in an effect
notes.detail: Creating it during render tripped `react-hooks/refs`. In an effect, StrictMode's double mount gets a fresh controller and the cleanup always disposes. The counter-argument: `start` reads `controller.current`, which is null before the first effect; a press can't arrive before then.

notes.title: The Dead zone counts scroll too
notes.detail: A scroll during a pending press can start the Drag, since the Note would otherwise jump when the pointer finally moves. The spec doesn't say either way.

notes.title: `useDrag` is excluded from the coverage gate
notes.detail: Node can't run it without jsdom, which the spec rules out. The browser tests drive every line of it with a real mouse in Chromium and Firefox.

notes.title: Real mouse input, through the scaled iframe
notes.detail: Vitest scales the 1024×768 test iframe into a smaller window, so `test/browserCommands.ts` maps each client point by the iframe's box and scale. A first version of the edge test moved the pointer out of the window and flaked in Firefox; it now stays over the top bar.
